functional.text: Hall call: a person on a floor presses up or down; one car is assigned and stops there going that way.
Car call: inside a car, pressing a floor button adds that destination to the car's stops.
A bank of 4 cars serves 20 floors; each hall call is assigned to exactly one car.
The dispatching policy can be changed (e.g. a rush-hour policy) without editing the controller.

non_functional.text: Safety: an overloaded car (over capacity / weight) or a car with open doors never moves; emergency stop overrides everything.
No starvation: every request is served in bounded time.
Requests arrive concurrently from many floors while cars move.

assumptions.text: 20 floors, 4 cars, 8 people / 640 kg per car.

out_of_scope.text: Motor control hardware, fire-service mode, destination-dispatch keypads.

api.notes: Hall call; the strategy picks the car, the car gets a stop.
Car call from the inside panel.
Safety controls; override the stop list.
Swap the dispatching policy at runtime.

data.name: Request
data.fields: floor, direction: Direction | None, source: HALL | CAR, created_at
data.why: One button press; direction is None for car calls.

data.name: ElevatorCar
data.fields: id, current_floor, direction, state: CarState, load_kg, up_stops (min-heap), down_stops (max-heap)
data.why: Everything the dispatcher needs to score a car, and the car's own stop list.

data.name: ElevatorController
data.why: The single place hall calls arrive.

deep_dives.title: Dispatching hall calls to cars

options.name: FCFS to any idle car
options.cons: ignores cars already passing by; long waits

options.name: scored: nearest car heading toward the caller, penalise full cars

deep_dives.choice: DispatchStrategy interface; default NearestCarStrategy scores by distance and direction; RushHourStrategy parks idle cars at the lobby
deep_dives.why: The policy is what the building wants to tune, so it sits behind a strategy the controller depends on (open/closed, dependency inversion).

deep_dives.title: Ordering a car's stops

options.name: LOOK (sweep): up stops sorted ascending, down stops descending

deep_dives.choice: LOOK with an up min-heap and a down max-heap
deep_dives.why: The car keeps its direction while stops remain ahead, then reverses; every stop is reached within one round trip so nobody starves.

wrapup.bottlenecks: The controller is a single entry point for hall calls; it only scores snapshots and enqueues, so it stays cheap.
wrapup.failures: A car entering maintenance or emergency stop hands its hall calls back to the controller for reassignment.
wrapup.monitoring: Average and p95 wait time, trip time, reassignments, cars out of service.
wrapup.scale: Concurrency: one thread per car owns its movement loop; stops sit in a per-car lock-protected structure (add_stop takes the car lock), the controller reads immutable car snapshots and never moves a car. Growth: more cars are more workers; zoning or a rush-hour policy is just another strategy.
wrapup.future: Destination dispatch (choose floor in the lobby) as a different Request source and strategy; energy-saving idle parking.
